title: In a high-dimensional product graph, two isolated vertices of the random subgraph are typically at distance at least three
author: Sahar Diskin, Anna Geisler
work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the geometric separation lemma for isolated vertices in the random subgraph of a high-dimensional product graph (author lemma at source lines 489-491, label lem:isolates-far). Its proof (source lines 493-510) is a second-moment count whose content is the case distinction on the pair: for non-adjacent u and v the incident edge sets are disjoint and the isolation probability is (1-p)^(2d), while for adjacent pairs the sets overlap in exactly one edge, which changes the exponent to 2d-1 and has to be absorbed by a constant alpha_M before the union bound can be applied (proof lines 495-503). The counting step then uses the author's range for p, displayed as eq:mu-range and delivered as a context span, to convert alpha_M nd^2 (1-p)^(2d) into alpha_M d^(2+1/25)/n = o(1) (proof lines 504-508). The closing appeal is Markov's inequality. H2.
